atoms.core_message: The choices nobody sees are quietly building who we become.

lines: No one sees every choice we make.
Yet these invisible choices quietly build our character.
They shape the kind of friend we become. The kind of citizen we become. The kind of human being we become.

atoms.core_message: Your mind finds the fastest route on other people's roads; your heart points to what matters to you.

items.metaphor: Your mind is like Google Maps — it looks for the fastest, smartest route based on other people’s roads.
Your heart is like a compass — it quietly points you toward what truly matters to you, even when no road is visible.

atoms.core_message: A decision from the head and a decision from the heart are different in five ways.

pairs.head: What others want
pairs.heart: What do you know is inside

atoms.core_message: Your heart's voice is quiet, and you can feel it in your body.

lines: It doesn’t shout.
It doesn’t always give answers in words.
But you can feel it.
It might feel like a gentle tug in your chest.
Or like a tight knot when something feels wrong.
Or a peaceful warmth when something feels right.

atoms.core_message: Your heart voice is not the same as a feeling in the moment; it is calm, kind and steady.

content.text: Your heart voice is not about doing what you feel in the moment (like snapping or crying). It’s deeper than emotion — it’s calm, kind, steady. It doesn’t need to win. It just wants to be true.

atoms.core_message: A set of quiet questions to help you notice what your heart wants.

content.title: Mirror Time: Questions to Hear Your Heart
questions: Can you remember a time when your heart wanted one thing, but your mind or your friends told you to do something else?
What did you choose in the end?
How did it feel in your body?
What does your inner voice feel like?
Can you name your heart’s voice?
content.naming_prompt: Give it a fun or special name — like Captain Courage, Whisper Friend, Kind Light, or Wise Me.
content.sentence_stem: When I feel confused, I can listen to my [heart name]. It tells me…

atoms.core_message: Siya found the wrong tiffin in her bag, and had to decide whether to return it to the quiet girl or walk away.

lines: It was just after lunch when Siya opened her schoolbag and saw it — a stainless-steel tiffin, neatly packed, but not hers.
No one would know if I just left it there, Siya thought.
But something small inside her, like a flicker, didn’t sit right.
Their eyes met, just for a second. And then Siya looked away.

atoms.core_message: Heart moments show up in ordinary situations: in friendships, at home, online, in class, and when no one is watching.

items.situation: You’re in a group chat, and someone sends a mean joke about another kid.
items.mind_says: Just laugh. Don’t make it a big deal.
items.heart_says: That’s not fair. I wouldn’t want this done to me.
items.heart_moment: Will you join in or speak up?

items.situation: Your younger sibling accidentally breaks your favorite pen.
items.heart_says: She didn’t mean to. Remember when you broke Dad’s glasses once?
items.heart_moment: Can you stay kind, even when angry?

items.setting: On Social Media or Group Apps
items.situation: You want to post something that’ll get likes — but deep down, it’s not really you.
items.heart_moment: Is this true to who I am?

items.situation: You know the answer, but you’re afraid to raise your hand.
items.heart_moment: Will you be brave and speak, or stay silent and safe?

items.situation: You find money on the floor.
items.heart_moment: What will you do when no one will ever know?

atoms.core_message: What do you do when no one will ever know?

lines: You find money on the floor.
There’s no one around. No cameras.
content.question: What will you do when no one will ever know?

atoms.core_message: Choosing from the heart isn't about being perfect; it's about pausing, listening and choosing what feels most honest.

lines: Making heart-based decisions doesn’t mean being perfect.
It means learning to pause, listen, and choose what feels most honest inside.
The more you practice, the stronger it grows.

atoms.core_message: There is a quiet truth inside you, and all you have to do is listen.

content.quote: There will always be noise around you — rules, advice, pressure. But somewhere inside you, there is a quiet truth. Your heart already knows. All you have to do… is listen.

atoms.core_message: Relational intelligence is the superpower of understanding people.

lines: It’s called relational intelligence — and it’s the superpower of understanding people.
Relational intelligence means noticing how others feel, how your words affect them, and how to keep relationships healthy — even when things get tricky.

atoms.core_message: Relational intelligence means listening deeply, knowing your feelings, understanding differences and balancing Me and We.

items: Listening deeply — not just to words, but to tone, face, and silence.
Knowing your feelings so you don’t dump them on others.
Understanding differences — that not everyone thinks or feels like you.
Balancing “Me” and “We” — respecting others and yourself.

atoms.core_message: Your brain is a calculator; your relational intelligence is a mirror and a bridge.

lines: Your brain is like a calculator — it solves numbers.
Your relational intelligence is like a mirror and a bridge.
It reflects what’s inside you, and it connects you to others.

atoms.core_message: On his birthday, Aarav has to decide whether to go along to stay in the group or say something and risk rejection.

lines: It was Aarav’s birthday.
Dev and Samar were already sitting in the birthday seat.
Go along with Dev to stay in the group — even if it felt unfair.
Or say something, even if it risks rejection.
content.closing_question: What do you think Aarav should do?

atoms.core_message: Relational intelligence shows up in class, in group chats, at lunch, at home and when you mess up.

items.situation: A friend gives the wrong answer. The class giggles.
items.relational_moment: Being smart without making others feel small.
Do you stay silent? Or text them later and say, “Hey, you, okay?”

items.situation: A quieter classmate walks by and seems to want to join in.
items.relational_moment: Do you notice? Do you scoot over and make space?

items.situation: Your sibling starts yelling. Your parent is tired. You feel stuck in between.
items.relational_moment: Can you stay calm, speak clearly, or even be the one who listens first?

items.situation: You interrupt a friend. Forget their birthday. Say something without thinking.
items.relational_moment: Can you own it and say, “I’m sorry— I didn’t mean to hurt you”?

atoms.core_message: It makes you someone others trust, respect and feel safe with.

lines: Aware of how you impact others
Willing to repair when needed
Brave enough to show care and set boundaries
Relational intelligence is the kind of intelligence that makes you someone others trust, respect, and feel safe with.

atoms.core_message: Questions to notice how you respond when someone ignores, interrupts or leaves someone out.

content.title: Mirror Time: Questions to Build Your “We” Power
questions: How do you usually respond when someone interrupts you, takes your seat, or ignores you?
Do you speak up, laugh it off, stay silent, or walk away?
What kind of friend are you?
The listener? The leader? The peacemaker? The honest one?
Who do you feel truly seen by?

atoms.core_message: Meher turned off a running tap and made a citizen's choice.

lines: She didn’t give a speech. She didn’t go to a protest.
She turned off the tap — and turned on her awareness.
For the first time, she wasn’t just brushing her teeth. She was making a choice. A quiet one. But a powerful one. A citizen’s choice.

atoms.core_message: Conscious citizenship flips taking into caring, me into we, and using the Earth into being part of it.

items: From me only → to we all
From using the Earth → to being part of it

atoms.core_message: The Earth isn't just something you live on; it's something you live with.

content.quote: The Earth isn’t a thing you live on — it’s something you live with.

atoms.core_message: The world needs people who care enough to act, not perfect people.

content.quote: The Earth doesn’t need more people who know stuff. It needs more people who care enough to act. You don’t have to be perfect. You have to show up.

atoms.core_message: Behind every person you admire stands an invisible team.

lines: Imagine a sports team preparing for an important match.
Behind every person you admire stands an invisible team that has helped shape their journey.
Understanding this invisible team helps us appreciate how connected our lives really are.

atoms.core_message: The people around us play different roles in helping us grow, even the ones who criticise.

items.role: They help you express yourself and let you be as you want to be.
They take you to see the other way possible; they are sent to you to see a new perspective which you would not otherwise know or wish to see.

items.who: Those who give you a chance
items.role: They believe in your ability and trust you to do what you are capable of. They give you a ground to play and showcase your potential.

atoms.core_message: We often judge people through a lens of our own ideas and experiences before we know them.

lines: Sometimes we make quick judgments about people based on how they look, what they wear, or what we’ve heard about them.
Sometimes we see people through a lens of our own ideas and experiences.

atoms.core_message: A short conversation a parent can have to help a child pause before judging someone who is quiet.

content.parent_prompt: Imagine you’re meeting a new student in your class. What if you decided they weren’t friendly just because they were quiet on the first day? How might that stop you from making a new friend?
content.parent_follow_up: So next time, let’s try to learn more about people before deciding what they’re like. Everyone has a story, just like you.

atoms.core_message: Positive self-talk means speaking to yourself with honesty, kindness and encouragement, not pretending problems don't exist.

lines: Have you ever noticed the voice inside your head when something goes wrong?
Sometimes it encourages us, and sometimes it criticizes us.
Positive self-talk does not mean pretending that problems do not exist. It means speaking to ourselves with honesty, kindness, and encouragement.
The way we talk to ourselves often becomes the foundation of how we face the world.

atoms.core_message: Five things you can say to yourself after a mistake.

sentences: Everyone makes mistakes, and that's how we learn.
It's okay not to be perfect.
I can try again and do better next time.
Failure is a part of success.
I am proud of myself for trying.

atoms.core_message: Five things you can say to yourself when peer pressure or negative comments hit.

content.situation: Dealing with Peer Pressure or Negative Comments
sentences: I am confident in my own choices.
Other people's opinions do not define me.
I can stand up for myself in a kind way.
I know what is right for me.
I am valuable just the way I am.

atoms.core_message: Five things you can say to yourself when you feel overwhelmed or stressed.

sentences: I can take one step at a time.
It's okay to ask for help when I need it.
I can handle this one moment at a time.
I am doing my best, and that's enough.
I can find ways to relax and feel better.

atoms.core_message: Five things you can say to yourself when anger or frustration builds.

sentences: I can calm myself with deep breaths.
It's okay to feel angry, but I can handle it.
I can express my feelings in healthy ways.
I am in control of my reactions.
I can choose to respond with kindness.

atoms.core_message: We notice what's missing by default; gratitude shifts attention to what supports us.

lines: We naturally notice what is missing, what is difficult, and what still needs improvement.
Gratitude helps us shift our attention toward the people, opportunities, experiences, and resources that support us every day.

atoms.core_message: Five simple ways to express gratitude.

items.name: Say Thank You
items.detail: Verbally express thanks whenever someone does something kind or helpful.

items.name: Write a Note
items.detail: Create thank-you notes or cards for teachers, friends, or family members.

items.name: Show Appreciation Through Actions
items.detail: Do something nice in return, such as helping with chores or sharing a toy.

items.name: Keep a Gratitude Journal
items.detail: Write down things you are thankful for each day.

items.name: Publicly Acknowledge
items.detail: Share gratitude in front of others, such as during family dinners or class discussions.

atoms.core_message: Gratitude doesn't need to be grand: three small things a day is enough to start.

lines: Begin by writing down three things you're grateful for each day.
Gratitude doesn’t need to be grand. Simple, sincere thanks go a long way.

atoms.core_message: People can't read our minds, so unspoken feelings turn into misunderstandings.

lines: No matter how much people care about us, they cannot read our minds.
Many misunderstandings arise when thoughts and feelings go unspoken.
Like any skill, communication improves with practice.

source_ref.locator: Communication: Building Bridges With Others, p.111

atoms.core_message: Whether 'they won't understand me' is true depends on what you do in the conversation.

content.reframe: Whether this is true or false would depend on what you do in the conversation.

atoms.core_message: Six things it takes to communicate what you feel.

items.name: Be Honest
items.detail: Clearly express your feelings without exaggeration.

items.name: Stay Calm
items.detail: Take deep breaths and try to stay calm when explaining how you feel.

items.name: Be Specific
items.detail: Explain exactly what is bothering you and why.

items.name: Use I Statements
items.detail: Focus on your own feelings rather than blaming others (e.g., I feel... instead of You made me feel...).

items.name: Listen
items.detail: Be open to the other person's perspective and listen to their response.

items.name: Ask for What You Need
items.detail: Clearly state what you need or how others can help you.

source_ref.locator: What does it really take to do communication?, pp.112-113

atoms.core_message: A model conversation for when a child feels overwhelmed by homework.

content.situation: Child is feeling overwhelmed with homework.
content.child_opens: Mom, I feel really overwhelmed with my homework today. It's so much, and I don't know where to start.
content.parent_responds: I understand; it can be tough sometimes. Can you show me what you have to do? Let's break it down into smaller tasks together.
content.parent_next_step: Let's tackle one subject at a time. How about we start with math, spend 30 minutes on it, and then take a short break?
content.child_closes: That sounds better. I think I can manage that.

atoms.core_message: How to tell a sibling you feel left out, and what a good reply sounds like.

content.situation: Child feels left out during playtime.
content.child_opens: Hey, can I talk to you for a minute? I feel like I'm being left out when you play with your friends.
content.sibling_responds: I'm sorry, I didn't realize you felt that way. Why don't you join us? What do you want to play?
content.child_asks: I'd like to play tag with you all. Can we do that?
content.sibling_closes: Sure, I'll let everyone know. Thanks for telling me how you feel.

atoms.core_message: What a parent can say when a child is sad and doesn't know why.

content.situation: Child feels sad and doesn't know why.
content.child_opens: Mom, I feel really sad today, but I don't know why.
content.parent_responds: It's okay to feel sad sometimes, even if you don't know why. Do you want to talk about anything that might be bothering you, or do you need a hug?
content.parent_closes: Remember, it's okay to have days like this. If you want to talk more later, I'm here for you.

atoms.core_message: What makes a hero is the choices they make, not their powers.

lines: The most important thing about a hero is not their powers—it is the choices they make.
A hero is not someone who never faces problems; a hero is someone who continues moving forward even when life becomes difficult.
heroes are not born; they are built, one choice at a time, one challenge at a time, and one lesson at a time.

atoms.core_message: You don't need a cape to be a hero; every day offers a chance.

content.quote: You do not need a cape to become a hero. Every day gives you opportunities to act like one.

atoms.core_message: Real heroes choose honesty over cheating, kindness over cruelty, learning over excuses and courage over fear.

content.lead: Every time you choose honesty over cheating, kindness over cruelty, learning over excuses, or courage over fear, you are practicing what real heroes do.

atoms.core_message: A little seed was told it was too small, believed in itself, and bloomed.

lines: Every day, it heard the tall trees whisper, "You are too small to grow like us." But the little seed believed in itself.
With each passing day, it pushed through the soil, soaking in sunlight and rain.
content.lesson: Believe in yourself, even when others doubt you. Self-confidence can help you achieve great things.

atoms.core_message: Confidence is believing you can keep going even when things go wrong.

content.quote: Confidence is not believing that nothing will go wrong. Confidence is believing that you can keep going even when things do.

atoms.core_message: Fear and doubt may always exist, but they don't have to control your choices.

lines: "You are too young."
"You are not good enough."
"You will never make it."
They did not disappear immediately, but they lost their power over him.
Fear and doubt may always exist, but they do not have to control our choices.

atoms.core_message: Not every thought deserves to be believed; growth can begin by rethinking what we assume is true.

lines: not every thought deserves to be believed.
Sometimes growth begins when we are willing to rethink what we assume is true.

atoms.core_message: The tools you found were built by you; the compass only reminded you to trust them.

content.quote: You did not find them. You built them.
content.follow_up: The compass only reminded you to trust the tools already inside you.

atoms.core_message: Everyone faces challenges; the difference is in the tools we use.

lines: The difference is not in the challenges themselves. The difference is in the tools we use to face them.
The journey was never about reaching the end of the forest.
It was about becoming the person capable of walking through it.

atoms.core_message: Four inner tools in your Superhero Tool Kit: awareness, observation, self-reflection and critical thinking.

items.meaning: helps you notice what is happening within you and around you.
teaches you to pay attention before jumping to conclusions.
helps you learn from your experiences and understand yourself better.
helps you question information, examine evidence, and make thoughtful decisions.

atoms.core_message: Five tools for acting on what you know: values, communication, gratitude, courage and patience.

items.meaning: act as your compass, guiding you toward what is right and meaningful.
allows you to express your thoughts, feelings, and needs while understanding others.
reminds you to appreciate the people, opportunities, and experiences that support your journey.
helps you take action even when you feel uncertain or afraid.
reminds you that meaningful growth takes time and that great things are often built one small step at a time.

atoms.core_message: The tools grow stronger only when you use them, like muscles.

lines: These tools are not meant to sit on a shelf. They become stronger every time you use them.
Just as muscles grow through exercise, these qualities grow through practice.
The wisdom lies in knowing which tool to use and when.

atoms.core_message: The book is only tools; you are the one who changes your life.

content.quote: This book was never meant to change your life. You are the one who changes your life.
content.follow_up: Like any tool, they become useful only when you choose to use them.

source_ref.locator: A Letter To The Hero Reading This Book, p.128

atoms.core_message: Confidence, doubt, success and mistakes all come with life, and that is normal.

lines: There will be days when you feel confident.
There will be days when you doubt yourself.
There will be successes.
There will be mistakes.
That is normal.
That is life.

atoms.core_message: Growth is about becoming a little wiser, kinder and stronger than yesterday.

lines: growth is not about becoming perfect.
Growth is about becoming a little wiser, a little kinder, and a little stronger than you were yesterday.

atoms.core_message: Keep asking, learning, helping, thinking for yourself, being curious, and being you.

lines: Keep asking questions.
Keep learning.
Keep helping others.
Keep thinking for yourself.
Keep being curious.
Most importantly, keep being you.

atoms.core_message: The world doesn't need another copy of someone else; it needs the best version of you.

content.quote: The world does not need another copy of someone else. The world needs the best version of you.
